why.why: Coronary angiography reveals only mild stenosis, and the expert analysis concludes that the findings favor myocarditis or vasospasm rather than a metabolic disorder. Although missing metabolic tests prevent complete exclusion, the cumulative cardiac evidence lowers confidence in an alcohol-related metabolic disorder from 0.2 to 0.15.

Laboratory and radiology expert analyses both conclude that the ECG abnormalities, mild stenosis on angiography, and normal troponin support an alcohol-related cardiac event as the leading diagnosis. The specific mechanism is most consistent with alcohol-induced coronary vasospasm. Confirmatory testing remains unavailable, so confidence is raised modestly from 0.8 to 0.85.
